About the Report
Our Approach to 
Reporting
At Metropolis Healthcare Limited 
(“Metropolis” or “MHL” or “the Company”), we are committed to upholding the highest standards of corporate disclosure and stakeholder communication. This Annual Report presents a holistic, transparent, and balanced overview of our performance for the financial year ended March 31, 2025. It offers insights into our strategy, business model, governance, risks, and performance across financial and non-financial parameters, reflecting how we create and sustain value for our stakeholders over time.
Basis of Reporting
This report has been prepared with the intent to inform and engage a broad spectrum of stakeholders, including shareholders, customers, partners, regulators, employees, and the communities we serve. It is guided by the principles of connectivity, materiality, consistency, and strategic focus to enhance the quality and relevance of disclosures.
Frameworks and 
Guidelines
The contents of this report 
are primarily guided by the International Integrated Reporting <IR> Framework developed by the IFRS Foundation (formerly the International Integrated Reporting Council - IIRC). In addition, it complies with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) requirements, the Companies Act, 2013. This multi-framework approach reflects our commitment to global best practices in transparency, governance, and stakeholder accountability.
Value Creation at 
Metropolis
The report outlines how Metropolis 
creates value through the effective use and management of six interdependent capitals:An in-depth analysis of the Company’s business model, strategic pillars, scientific innovation, and governance practices demonstrates how these capitals contribute to our long-term sustainability and stakeholder value.
Reporting Scope and 
Boundary
This report covers the activities 
of Metropolis Healthcare Limited and its subsidiaries for the period April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025. It includes both financial and non-financial disclosures that reflect our performance and value creation across the six capitals. The consolidated financial statements have been independently audited and prepared in compliance with the applicable Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS).
Assurance
The disclosures presented in this report have been reviewed and approved by the Company’s Board of Directors and its committees. While the statutory financial statements have undergone external audit, the non-financial information presented has not been subjected to third-party assurance.
Feedback
We value stakeholder feedback and view it as an essential input in improving the quality and relevance of our reporting. We invite you to share your suggestions, questions, or comments by writing to us at:

WITH CLARITY OF 
PURPOSE AND THE CONFIDENCE OF EXPERIENCE, WE ARE REIMAGINING DIAGNOSTICS TO MEET THE NEEDS OF A CHANGING INDIA.
India’s healthcare 
landscape is transforming rapidly—driven by rising health awareness, a growing demand for preventive care, and the seamless integration of digital technologies into everyday medicine. At Metropolis, we are not just adapting to this change—we are leading it. Backed by over four decades of scientific excellence, we are reshaping diagnostics with a sharp focus on precision, accessibility, and patient-first  outcomes.
Evolve. Expand. Energize
Reimagining Diagnostics for a Healthier Tomorrow

From Diagnostics to Personalized, Patient-Centric Care
We are evolving our model to keep pace with a more informed, 
digital, and discerning patient. Every touchpoint—whether in a lab, at home, or online—is being reimagined to simplify and enrich the diagnostic experience. From AI-led reporting and mobile-first journeys to precision-driven test innovation, we are enabling proactive health management that is intuitive, insightful, and impactful.
Our evolution isn’t just digital—it’s deeply human. At every step, 
we are guided by empathy, clinical integrity, and a relentless pursuit of excellence.
Scaling Access with Intent, Reach with Relevance
Metropolis today operates in 750+ towns across India—with strongholds in metros and growing reach across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Our expansion strategy is anchored in agility and intent: combining company-owned centres, franchise networks, and digital channels to deliver consistent, high
-
quality diagnostics wherever the patient is.
As we enter new markets, we do so with a deep understanding of local healthcare needs—balancing scale with sensitivity, and growth with governance.
Accelerating Innovation, Empowering People, 
Elevating Impact
At the heart of our transformation is an energized core—one 
that combines cutting-edge science, data-driven systems, and a culture of ownership. From lab automation to digital platforms, from talent development to sustainability, we are building a future-ready organization driven by speed, precision, and resilience.
Our ambition is bold yet grounded: to elevate Metropolis 
from India’s No. 2 diagnostics chain to the most trusted, scientifically advanced, and patient-centric healthcare diagnostics brand in the country.
Looking Ahead
We remain deeply committed to our purpose—delivering diagnostics that are accurate, accessible, and accountable. As we evolve in tune with patient needs, expand access across communities, and energize every facet of our operations, our focus is clear: to shape the future of healthcare through precision and compassion.
It’s good to be sure.
It’s time to reimagine what diagnostics can do.EVOLVE

At the Heart of Diagnostics.  
At the Forefront of Innovation.Metropolis at a Glance
For over four decades, Metropolis 
Healthcare has been synonymous with trust, precision, and innovation. What began as a single lab in 1981 has evolved into one of India’s most respected diagnostic networks—serving over 20 million patients annually across India, Africa and few other international markets.
Our strength lies in bridging clinical depth with 
technological agility. Through AI-driven platforms, digital-first patient journeys, and home-based diagnostics, we are making healthcare more seamless, personal, and proactive. Consistently ranked in the top 1% globally with CAP* proficiency scores at 99%, we continue to set benchmarks in scientific accuracy and quality assurance.
As we expand, we continue to invest in our 
future—building capability through MiLES (Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education and Skilling), enhancing clinical excellence through i-MAB (Internal Medical Advisory Board), and integrating acquisitions to strengthen leadership in specialized diagnostics.
Our purpose is simple but profound: To deliver 
diagnostics that are accurate, accessible, and empathetic, improving lives every step of the way.
*CAP - College of American Pathologists

A Refreshed Brand for a Renewed Purpose
In FY  2024-25, Metropolis Healthcare unveiled a refreshed brand identity—one that reflects the enduring strength of our 
legacy and the clarity of our future aspirations. As our network expands and patient relationships deepen, this strategic 
evolution redefines how we convey our promise of precision and compassion to the world.
Through this refreshed identity, Metropolis reaffirms its role as a trusted health partner—bridging the gap between technology and humanity, science and sensitivity, data and decisions.
More than just a visual upgrade, this transformation is 
foundational. It strengthens how we build deeper patient relationships, enhance brand trust, and reinforce our leadership in the diagnostics space.This new positioning captures our dual commitment: delivering diagnostics grounded in scientific rigour, while fostering empathy at every step of the patient journey. It reflects a growing need among health-conscious individuals—to feel seen, supported, and empowered in their healthcare decisions.
Unlike many other service providers that focus solely on 
outcomes, Metropolis is built on the belief that diagnosing with the heart is essential for a healthier tomorrow.“Empowering your health decisions with precision and compassion”
At the heart of this new identity lies our core brand idea, which guides every touchpoint of the Metropolis experience—internally and externally.

Expanding Reach, Enhancing 
Patient Access Geographic Presence
INDIA
In FY25, we strengthened our national footprint through a strategic mix of organic growth and targeted acquisitions. 
Our network now spans over 750 towns across 28 states and 7 Union Territories, enabled by a flexible, asset-light model. During the year, we added 11 new laboratories and acquired Core Diagnostics, a leading cancer-focused testing player based in Delhi NCR. As part of our ‘String of Pearls’ strategy to reinforce our presence in North India, we completed the acquisitions of Dr. Ahuja’s Pathology & Imaging Centre (Dehradun, Uttarakhand) and Scientific Pathology (Agra, Uttar Pradesh) in Q1 FY26. These expansions will further deepen our scientific capabilities, strengthen our regional leadership, and will enable us to serve more communities with precision diagnostics—driving stronger revenue contribution from high-growth markets.

AFRICA & BEYOND
We have established a strong presence in Africa over the past decade, with company-managed laboratories and

In addition, we serve a diverse portfolio of B2B laboratory clients across 12 international markets, including Abu Dhabi, Bangladesh, Congo, Dubai, Maldives, Mauritius, Nepal, Nigeria, Sri Lanka, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, and Zimbabwe. Scaling with Strength 
and PurposeLetter from the Chairperson
AT EVERY STEP OF OUR JOURNEY , OUR 
GOAL REMAINED CLEAR: TO DELIVER 
ACCURATE, EMPATHETIC, AND IMPACTFUL DIAGNOSTICS THAT ENABLE BETTER HEAL TH OUTCOMES AND CREATE GREAT VALUE FOR SHAREHOLDERS WHILST DOING IT.
DEAR SHAREHOLDERS,
As I reflect on FY 2024-25, it is 
clear that this has been a year of purposeful transformation for Metropolis Healthcare. In a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, we chose not merely to respond to change, but to actively shape it. This year, we strengthened our core, expanded our reach through strategic moves, and infused new energy into our operations and culture. These actions were not just tactical; they were deeply aligned with our long-term vision of redefining diagnostics in India and beyond.
Our journey over the last year 
has been guided by a conscious effort to evolve into a more agile, digitally empowered organization. We enhanced our capabilities and national footprint, while maintaining our unwavering focus on scientific excellence, customer centricity, and operational discipline. At every step of our journey, our goal remained clear: to deliver accurate, empathetic, 
18
Annual Report 2024-25
=== page 22 ===
and impactful diagnostics that 
enable better health outcomes and create great value for shareholders whilst doing it.
Evolving Roles, Enduring Vision
This year also marked a significant milestone in our leadership journey. Our Founder and Chairman, Dr. Sushil Shah, transitioned to the role of Chairman Emeritus. His vision—that diagnostics should bridge anxiety and assurance—continues to serve as our guiding principle. Dr. Shah’s legacy of scientific rigor and ethical leadership is deeply embedded in the culture of Metropolis. He remains an integral part of our Board, offering his valuable insights and direction as we chart the next phase of our growth. 
In line with this transition, the 
Board entrusted me with the role of Executive Chairperson during the early part of the financial year, in addition to my existing responsibilities. Over the past two decades, I have had the privilege of leading Metropolis through multiple phases of evolution, from a single-lab entity to a publicly listed institution, now the second-largest diagnostics player in India with national presence and global quality benchmarks. This leadership transition reaffirms our commitment to continuity in governance and long-term strategic stewardship.
Navigating a Changing 
Landscape
India’s healthcare sector continues 
to evolve rapidly and is now valued at over USD 370 billion*. Within this expanding ecosystem, diagnostics has emerged as a critical pillar—enabling early detection, accurate clinical decisions, and improved patient outcomes. The post-pandemic years saw a sharp influx of new entrants, particularly in wellness and home-testing, many of whom adopted price-led strategies. However, the market is now transitioning toward greater consolidation and maturity—placing increased value on quality, trust, and scientific integrity. With rising awareness, chronic disease prevalence, and demand for speed and precision, the diagnostics sector is poised to grow at 8–10% CAGR through FY28.
Metropolis has navigated this 
changing landscape with clarity and conviction. Over the last four years, we have undergone a significant transformation, anchored in strategic investments, bold execution, and a clear intent to build a resilient, future-ready organization. We expanded our lab footprint by nearly 90 labs and scaled our network of owned Patient Service Centers from ~251 (FY22) to over 530, while modernizing front-end platforms and automating back-end lab processes. These foundational changes have materially strengthened our B2C capabilities and positioned us for sustained value creation. 
As part of this transformation, we 
also made a conscious decision to defocus from the Institutional business (including some that were profitable). This strategic pivot allowed us to reallocate capital and resources toward building scalable, consumer-facing capabilities—across technology, talent, and geographic reach. While this investment-led scale-up phase led to a temporary increase in costs, it has created a stronger operating base for future growth.
We are also witnessing a broader 
shift within the industry—from unorganised to organised players—which has expanded the formal market but distributed revenue among more players. Competition has moderated, with fewer instances of irrational pricing and aggressive new entrants. Many competitors are increasingly focused on wellness and the tail end of the illness spectrum. At Metropolis, we remain committed on the head of the illness business—critical diagnostics that demand trust, quality, and scientific depth.Driving Resilient Financial 
Performance
FY 2024–25 was a year of consistent 
and well-balanced growth for Metropolis. Revenues grew 12% year-on-year to `
 1,331 crore, with 
B2C growing b
y 17% and B2B by 12% 
on a Y-o-Y basis. The overall growth was moderated to 12% due to a decline in the Institutional Business, which we are actively de-focusing; otherwise, it would have stood at 14%. Adjusted EBITDA increased by 14% to `
 325 crore (on an adjust
ed 
basis excluding one-time acquisition-related costs incurred in the fourth quarter), while profit after tax rose 26% to `
 
161 crore.
The TruHealth wellness portfolio recorded robust growth of 24%, and the Specialty diagnostics segment expanded by 13%—together serving as key engines of differentiated growth. We also achieved steady volume expansion, processing over 26.4 million tests across 12.7 million patient visits, along with a 6% improvement in revenue per patient. These outcomes reaffirm the strength of our strategy, our alignment with emerging healthcare priorities, and our ability to scale profitably in a dynamic market—while continuing to earn the trust of patients and clinicians across the country.
Accelerating Growth through 
Strategic Acquisitions
At Metropolis, acquisitions have 
always been a strategic lever, not just for expanding scale, but for deepening scientific expertise, enhancing regional strength, and delivering consistent quality to patients. A defining milestone came nearly four years ago with the acquisition of Chennai-based Hitech Diagnostics, our first large-scale regional buyout that fortified our position as a B2C leader in South India and demonstrated our ability to integrate effectively while preserving local strengths.
19
Corporate Overview Statutory Reports Financial Statements
Metropolis Healthcare LimitedLetter from the Chairperson
=== page 23 ===
Building on that foundation, 
FY 2024–25 marked a breakthrough year as we extended our acquisition-led growth into North India through our focused “String of Pearls” strategy, an approach centered on acquiring high-quality, culturally aligned regional leaders to strengthen our national footprint. During the year, we completed the acquisition of Core Diagnostics, a leading Delhi-NCR-based pan India player specializing in oncology and genomics. In the first quarter of FY 2025-26, we further expanded with the acquisitions of Scientific Pathology in Agra and Dr. Ahuja’s Pathology & Imaging Centre in Dehradun—both established B2C brands with deep-rooted equity in Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, respectively.
Together, these additions have 
significantly strengthened our presence in North India, with the region’s contribution to overall revenues rising from 8% to nearly 14–15%. As we integrate these businesses into the Metropolis ecosystem, our focus remains on unlocking synergies across digital infrastructure, operational excellence, and clinical expertise, laying the foundation for long-term value creation and sustained leadership in high-potential markets.Science, Innovation, and Digital 
Acceleration
One of the most fulfilling aspects 
of this year has been the visible convergence of science, quality, and technology. By aligning our scientific and quality functions, we have created a more unified, precision-driven diagnostic ecosystem—one that delivers measurable outcomes across patient and clinician touchpoints. 
I want to sincerely appreciate our 
scientific and technical teams for their relentless commitment to clinical excellence. Their efforts have brought forth next-generation diagnostic offerings, from molecular and NGS-based panels to AI-supported reporting tools. The addition of Core Diagnostics has given further momentum to our genomics and oncology capabilities, positioning us at the forefront of precision medicine in India.
On the technology front, we have 
embedded intelligent automation, ERP-CRM integrations, and AI-led workflow optimization across lab and service functions. These initiatives support not just scale, but responsiveness, traceability, and personalization. As we prepare for the next frontier, I am confident that this synergy of science, digital intelligence, and quality systems will help us continue delivering industry-defining diagnostic care—accessible, accurate, and ahead of the curve.
Empowering People, Enriching 
Culture
People and culture remain at the 
heart of everything we do. Our teams are the architects of our patient-first promise. Whether it is elevating quality benchmarks through our proprietary Quality Index or maintaining consistently high Net Promoter Scores, our workforce continues to raise the bar for diagnostics in India. With a gender ratio of ~45% women and a clear roadmap toward achieving 50:50 gender balance by 2028, we continue to make steady progress in our diversity journey.
We also recognize that investing in 
talent means building for the future. While we continue to empower our employees through structured learning and development programs, we are equally focused on expanding industry capabilities. The Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education and Skilling (MiLES) has emerged as a key initiative in this direction—training the next generation of healthcare professionals with advanced competencies and aligned with India’s national skilling mission. Through MiLES, we are not only investing in the professionals of tomorrow but also reinforcing Metropolis’ role as a knowledge-led leader in diagnostics. 
Creating Impact Beyond the 
Business
Our social responsibility goes 
far beyond diagnostics. Through the Metropolis Foundation, our CSR arm, we continue to make a meaningful impact in public health and community well-being. Our MedEngage platform has scaled significantly this year, awarding 365 scholarships—63% to women, 49% to students from aspirational districts, and 43% as research grants, marking a 50% increase over the previous year.
Among key initiative, the Adolescent 
Reproductive and Sexual Health (ARSH) program has now reached over 2.2 lakh adolescents across Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. Supported by our ‘Too Shy to Ask’ app, we are enabling young individuals to make informed health decisions. Additionally, we conducted over 300 screening and awareness

Charting the Next Phase: 
Consolidation, Focus, and  
Value-Centric Growth
As we transition into the next 
phase of our journey, our strategic priorities are clearly defined. With core infrastructure in place, the emphasis now shifts from expansion to disciplined execution, tighter cost control, and automation-led productivity—enabling us to drive sustainable profitability across the network.
Over the next three years, we will 
recalibrate our approach to growth. Asset-heavy investments in labs and technology will be paused, allowing us to consolidate recent expansions and extract full value from our existing infrastructure. Capital expenditure will be more calibrated, with internal accruals directed toward high-quality, financially accretive acquisitions and strengthening in-house capabilities.
Our ambition is to evolve into 
a fully tech-enabled, leaner organization—focused on the most critical and high-value segments of the illness business. At the same time, we will continue to broaden our ancillary services to keep the patient at the center of our ecosystem—enhancing value through increased revenue per test (RPT) and integrated experiences. While volume growth remains important, our focus will be on striking the right balance between scale and value, especially in specialist-driven diagnostics where clinical relevance, accuracy, and trust are paramount.FY26 will be a year of strategic consolidation. We will focus on standardizing operations and harmonizing clinical practices across acquired entities to ensure consistency, quality, and compliance. From FY27 onward, we aim to enter a new phase of growth—anchored in operational maturity, stronger governance, and focused execution for both top-line and bottom-line expansion.
Strategic Governance for a 
Future-Ready Metropolis
As we pursue our ambitions, we 
remain firmly anchored in strong governance. Toward the end of the last quarter, we welcomed two distinguished Independent Directors—Mr. Rehan Khan and Ms. Purvi Sheth—who bring deep expertise in healthcare strategy and people leadership, respectively. Their perspectives will further strengthen our Board as we navigate the next phase of growth with enhanced agility and foresight.
In line with our leadership continuity 
plan, our CEO Mr. Surendran Chemmenkotil has been elevated to Managing Director, reinforcing operational execution at a critical juncture. In this role, Surendran will continue to work closely with me and the Board to drive sustainable growth, integrate strategic investments, accelerate innovation, and contribute meaningfully to the broader healthcare ecosystem. His elevation reflects our confidence in his ability to create long-term shareholder value while staying aligned with Metropolis’ mission of delivering trusted, high-quality diagnostics.
Note of Gratitude 
FY 2024–25 has been a year of momentum, discipline, and clarity. I am deeply grateful to our teams, customers, partners, and shareholders for their unwavering support. I also extend my sincere appreciation to our doctors, employees, and Board members for their dedication and contributions throughout the year.
We have laid a strong foundation for 
strategic and sustainable progress in the years ahead. I would also like to acknowledge the continued support of local, state, and national governments across the regions we serve. Together, we are not just adapting to a changing healthcare landscape—we are helping shape it. With collective ambition and a firm commitment to excellence, I am confident that Metropolis will continue to lead the future of diagnostics in India.

Enhanced Customer Experience

On the B2B front, we sharpened 
our institutional business strategy to enhance profitability and engagement. By exiting low-margin contracts and optimizing engagement models, we laid the groundwork for more sustainable and mutually beneficial partnerships with hospitals, clinics, and government health programs. At the same time, our ambition to be more than a diagnostics provider led us to expand into adjacent healthcare services. We introduced basic radiology services—such as X-ray, ECG, and sonography—at select patient service centres, and enabled hybrid consultation models that combine digital convenience with physical doctor access. These offerings have strengthened our ability to support patients across the care continuum, particularly in chronic and lifestyle conditions.
From an operational perspective, 
we achieved meaningful efficiencies through improved sample logistics, centralized inventory systems, better procurement terms, and greater automation. These gains allowed us to reduce costs, enhance accuracy and turnaround time, and reinvest in expanding patient services and reinforcing our operational backbone.

QUALITY CUL TURE
Driven by Leadership, Measured by Science
At Metropolis, quality is not a standalone metric—it is deeply embedded in our values, behaviors, and systems. Our 
quality culture is championed from the top, reinforced through structured cascades, real-time KPIs, and technology-backed governance.
Our central Quality Assurance (QA) team maintains objectivity and rigor by operating independently of operations 
and reporting directly to the Managing Director. This structure ensures transparent benchmarking, enables proactive risk mitigation, and supports faster decision-making.
We also leverage digital dashboards, internal audits, and root-cause analytics to ensure adherence to global 
standards such as NABL, CAP, and EQAS.
In FY25, we further institutionalized this ethos by establishing a robust Quality Index anchored in 10 measurable 
parameters. This framework provides real-time insights and actionable visibility into every layer of our operations—ensuring that quality is not just tracked, but actively improved.

Launched in 2018, MedEngage is 
Metropolis Foundation’s flagship medical outreach program designed to nurture the next generation of Indian healthcare professionals. Aligned with the UN SDGs and India's healthcare education goals, MedEngage provides financial support, academic enrichment, and research opportunities for MBBS and postgraduate medical students across India.
More than a scholarship initiative, 
MedEngage is a holistic platform that supports students through a multi-dimensional approach—scholarships, research grants, observerships, laboratory tours, internships, and MedTalk webinars. It aims to bridge the gap between medical education and hands-on experience, promoting inclusivity, innovation, and leadership across India’s evolving healthcare landscape.

Annual Report 2024-25Management Discussion and Analysis
GLOBAL ECONOMY
The global economy navigated a challenging environment 
in 2024, shaped by shifting geopolitical dynamics and changing market patterns. It expanded by 3.3% year-over-year, indicating steady though moderate growth. Advanced economies posted a 1.8% increase, while Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs) showed continued resilience with a 4.3% rise. The US economy held firm, supported by a strong labour market and strong domestic demand. In contrast, the Eurozone grappled with structural hurdles, particularly in energy-intensive industries. India and Southeast Asia stood out, driven by robust domestic consumption, digital advancements and infrastructure development. China’s recovery faced obstacles, including a slowdown in the property sector and softer external demand. The health of the global economy and the strength of healthcare systems were deeply interconnected, as economic stability drove healthcare investments, while robust healthcare underpinned workforce productivity and economic growth.

Source: IMF April 2025 Report
The global economic outlook for 2025 presented a blend 
of challenges and opportunities, influenced by evolving trade dynamics and shifting policy landscapes. Advanced economies were expected to achieve their inflation targets earlier, while Emerging Market and Developing Economies (EMDEs), notably China and India, were projected to sustain healthy growth momentum. However, the imposition of new tariffs by the US and corresponding retaliatory measures introduced fresh risks to global trade, with the potential to elevate inflation and temper growth. Global GDP is expected to grow by 2.8% year-on-year in 2025 and by 3.0% in 2026, signalling a gradual moderation compared to the stronger pace observed over the previous two years. Growth in advanced economies was projected at 1.4% in 2025 and 1.5% in 2026, indicating a period of moderate expansion, while EMDEs were expected to deliver more robust growth of 3.7% and 3.9% respectively. Despite the uncertainties, technological advancement and supportive policy measures were anticipated to underpin economic resilience. In this evolving landscape, the strength and resilience of healthcare systems remained equally critical, playing a pivotal role in safeguarding human capital and sustaining economic productivity.
INDIAN ECONOMY
India ranks as the world’s fifth-largest economy by total 
Gross Domestic Product (GDP), mirroring its expanding role in the global economy. However, uncertainty surrounding the national elections in early FY
 2024-25,
 
combined with weather-related setbacks that affected construction and manufacturing in the following quarter, led to a softer-than-expected performance in gross fixed capital formation. Even with these headwinds, India has continued to demonstrate resilience, supported by robust macroeconomic conditions and an emphasis on sustainability and innovation throughout FY
 2024-25.
 
According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) second advance estimates, real GDP is projected to grow by 6.5% year-on-year in FY
 2024
-
25, following a 9.2% increase in FY
 2023-24.
On April 9, 2025, the R
eserve Bank of India’s Monetary 
Policy Committee (MPC) unanimously voted to reduce the repo rate by 25 basis points, lowering it from 6.25% to 6.0%. This move is intended to improve liquidity and support economic activity. The last rate adjustment occurred during the February 2025 policy meeting, where repo rate was reduced from 6.5% to 6.25%. Despite the reduction, the MPC retained its “accommodative” stance, signalling flexibility to respond to evolving economic and market conditions. Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation eased to 4.9% in FY

INDIAN HEAL THCARE INDUSTRY
India's healthcare sector stands at the cusp of a transformative phase in FY 2024-25, driven by a combination of increased public and private investments, progressive policy reforms, and demographic shifts. Healthcare expenditure in India is expected to grow from 3.3% of GDP to 5% of GDP by 2030, as projected by CareEdge’s April 2025 report.
The government's strategic focus on strengthening 
healthcare systems is clearly reflected in its FY

This growing demand is anticipated to drive investments across the healthcare value chain, including medical education, hospital infrastructure development, and digital health technologies. Noteworthy developments during FY 2024-25 include the doubling of medical seats, expansion of health insurance coverage, and the continuous addition of hospital beds, which are essential to building a resilient healthcare system. Between FY 2025-26 and FY 2027-28, India is expected to add between 25,000 and 30,000 new hospital beds, facilitated by contributions from both public and private sectors. The focus on medical education has been reinforced with targeted investments in the expansion of nursing and medical colleges, aiming to bridge the gap in the healthcare workforce. While challenges persist, the overall outlook for India’s healthcare sector remains optimistic, backed by consistent investments, strategic initiatives, and a commitment to improving healthcare access and quality.

DIAGNOSTICS INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
India’s diagnostics industry has emerged as a critical 
pillar of the healthcare ecosystem, enabling early detection, accurate diagnosis, and informed treatment decisions. Despite its pivotal role—contributing to over 70% of clinical decision-making—diagnostics remains significantly under-penetrated, accounting for just 6% of total healthcare spending. The industry was valued at approximately US$ 12 billion in FY24 and is expected to grow at a robust CAGR of 8-10% through FY28, driven by increasing healthcare awareness, higher disease burden, rising demand for preventive testing, and a gradual shift toward organized, quality-centric service providers.
The market continues to be highly fragmented, with nearly 
85% of diagnostics services delivered by hospital-based or standalone unorganized labs. Organized players, although representing just 15% of the market, have consistently outperformed the industry with a CAGR of 12% over the past five years, supported by superior operational efficiencies, technology adoption, and brand trust. Quality remains a key differentiator, as only about 5% of India’s laboratories are NABL accredited, contributing to concerns 
=== page 75 ===
72
Annual Report 2024-25over accuracy and misdiagnosis—identified as the second 
leading cause of death in India between 2017–2019.
Segment-wise, pathology comprises 58% of the industry, 
valued at US$ 7.5 billion, and continues to witness steady growth with a shift toward specialized and high-value testing. Radiology, valued at US$ 5.4 billion, is increasingly gaining traction due to its critical role in managing chronic diseases and the government's focused investment in expanding radiology access through initiatives like the Free Diagnostics Services Initiative (FDSI). The emergence of tele-radiology and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for domestic equipment manufacturing are further propelling growth in this segment.
INDUSTRY OUTLOOK
Looking ahead, the Indian diagnostics sector is poised for sustained long-term growth, supported by a favorable convergence of healthcare demand, digital acceleration, and supportive policy measures. Rising incidences of non-communicable diseases—projected to account for over 70% of all deaths by 2030—alongside a growing emphasis on preventive healthcare, are expected to significantly boost testing volumes and value.
Preventive and wellness diagnostics, which currently 
constitute around 10–12% of the pathology market, are anticipated to grow at 18–20% CAGR, driven by increasing corporate wellness initiatives, wider insurance coverage, and heightened health consciousness among consumers. Furthermore, geographic expansion into tier 2 and tier 3 cities presents a compelling growth opportunity, as nearly two-thirds of the country's diagnostic test volumes originate from non-metro regions.
Amid this evolving landscape, organized diagnostics 
chains are well-positioned to lead the next wave of transformation by leveraging digital platforms, expanding hub-and-spoke networks, introducing advanced testing capabilities in genomics and molecular diagnostics, and maintaining a strong focus on quality and affordability. With superior return metrics, low regulatory risk, and a resilient business model, the diagnostics sector is expected to continue commanding premium valuations within the healthcare space.
GOVERNMENT INITIATIVES DRIVING DIAGNOSTICS 
INDUSTRY GROWTH
The Indian diagnostics industry continues to gain 
momentum, not only due to increasing healthcare awareness and disease burden, but also owing to strong policy interventions by the Government of India. A series of strategic programs have been launched to enhance accessibility, affordability, and quality of diagnostics across the country. These initiatives are accelerating structural changes within the sector and opening up long-term growth opportunities, particularly for organized players.
Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana 
(PM-JAY)—2018: PM-JAY is one of the world’s largest government-funded health insurance schemes, providing `
 5 lakh co
verage per family annually for secondary 
and tertiary care. With over 500 million beneficiaries, the program has stimulated demand for diagnostics by promoting structured treatment protocols and encouraging early detection at empanelled hospitals.
Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs)—2018 onwards: As 
part of Ayushman Bharat, HWCs are designed to deliver primary healthcare services, including basic diagnostics, to communities across India. With a target of 1,50,000 operational centres by 2025, this initiative strengthens preventive healthcare and creates direct demand for routine and point-of-care testing services.
Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM)—2021: ABDM 
is building a digital health ecosystem anchored by unique Health IDs and interoperable Electronic Health Records (EHRs). By facilitating seamless access to patients' diagnostic history, the initiative is expected to improve care coordination and enable more data-driven diagnostics.
PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission 
(PM-ABHIM)—2021: With a total outlay of `
 
64,200 
crore over FY
 2022-26, PM-
ABHIM focuses on enhancing 
diagnostics and surveillance infrastructure at all levels of the healthcare system. It includes the setup of block and district-level labs, addressing a critical gap in public health diagnostics capability.
Free Diagnostics Services Initiative (FDSI)—2015:  
Implemented under the National Health Mission, FDSI aims 
to provide essential pathology and radiology services at government health facilities, primarily through public-private partnerships (PPP). The initiative has gained strong traction, with steady increases in budget allocations by both central and state governments. The focus on radiology expansion, including the planned addition of 2,000 diagnostic centres, is expected to significantly enhance diagnostic coverage in underserved districts.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Medical 
Devices—2020: This scheme incentivizes the domestic manufacturing of advanced radiology and imaging equipment, such as CT, MRI, and PET machines. Beneficiaries include major players like Siemens, Trivitron, and Philips. The scheme reduces capital intensity for diagnostics providers and is expected to increase

COMPANY OVERVIEW
Metropolis Healthcare Limited (hereafter referred to as 
“Metropolis” or “the Company”) is one of India’s most trusted and advanced diagnostic service providers, with a legacy spanning over four decades. Established in 1981 and guided by visionary leadership, the Company has grown to become the second-largest and the most respected diagnostics chain in the country, offering best-in-class pathology services across India and Africa. Metropolis is synonymous with precision, quality, and compassion—delivering not just results, but reassurance to millions of patients.
With operations spanning 28 states, 7 Union Territories, 
and over 750 towns in India, Metropolis maintains a robust infrastructure of 210 clinical laboratories, over 4,500+ service network, and 10,000+ touchpoints. The Company serves a broad spectrum of customers, including individual patients, hospitals, corporates, and healthcare institutions, across both B2C and B2B segments. Its test portfolio encompasses more than 4,100 diagnostics and profiles, covering routine, advanced, and highly specialized areas such as oncology, molecular genomics, neurology, infectious diseases, and women and child health.
FY
 2024–25 was a landmark year f
or Metropolis, marked 
by significant strategic progress and the advancement 
of its refreshed brand vision. Under the overarching theme of “The Year of More”, the Company accelerated its Metropolis 3.0 transformation journey, strengthening its capabilities in scientific innovation, digital enablement, customer experience, and geographic reach.
Metropolis further reinforced its leadership in high-value 
precision diagnostics through the strategic acquisition of Core Diagnostics, enhancing capabilities in oncology and molecular testing. Additionally, the acquisitions of Scientific Pathology and Dr. Ahuja’s Pathology & Imaging Centre (DAPIC) expanded the Company’s B2C footprint and deepened its presence across North India. These acquisitions not only enhanced scale and network coverage but also aligned with Metropolis’ vision of bringing high-quality diagnostics closer to the consumer.
Innovation and digital transformation were central to the 
Company’s growth agenda. The launch of a new mobile application with real-time sample tracking, personalized dashboards, and AI-powered recommendations significantly enhanced the customer experience. A newly introduced B2B partner portal streamlined workflows and strengthened partner engagement. AI integration was extended into clinical areas as well, with the rollout of AI-driven diagnostic tools such as prostate cancer detection and Karyotyping, significantly reducing turnaround times and improving diagnostic accuracy.
During the year, Metropolis expanded its network rapidly—  
growing from approximately 300 towns in FY23 to over 
750 by the end of FY25. The Company inaugurated 51 new laboratories, particularly across Tier II and Tier III cities, and enhanced its international presence by launching a Regional Reference Lab in Nairobi, Kenya. These developments were supported by region-specific strategies, including competitive pricing, localized micro-marketing, and customized test offerings tailored to market needs.
On the scientific front, Metropolis introduced over 60 
new specialty tests across oncology, nephrology, chronic care, and preventive health during FY
 2024-25. The
 
establishment of Centres of Excellence for key specialties and the formation of an Internal Medical Advisory Board (I-MAB), comprising more than 50 subject matter experts, underscored the Company’s commitment to clinical excellence. Additionally, Metropolis engaged with over 70,000 clinicians through its Metrobot platform and published more than 20 peer-reviewed research articles, reinforcing its position as a thought leader in diagnostics.
As part of its commitment to workforce development 
and community engagement, Metropolis launched the Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education and Skilling (MiLES). This initiative bridges the gap between academic learning and practical diagnostic expertise. Through collaborations with leading academic institutions such as DY Patil (Deemed-to-be) University, Navi Mumbai, and Ratan Tata Maharashtra State Skills University, Metropolis is nurturing the next generation of laboratory professionals. The MiLES program offers eight UGC-recognized certified courses for DML T, B.Sc. ML T, and other laboratory professionals, including Advanced Clinical Chemistry, Hematopathology, Surgical Pathology, Molecular Pathology & Cytogenomics, and Quality Assurance in Laboratory Medicine. In addition, it provides one-year fellowship programs for post-MD and DNB professionals in specialized domains. The curriculum combines theoretical instruction, hands-on training, real-world case exposure, and research—guided by in-house subject matter experts. In parallel, community outreach initiatives such as the Adolescent Reproductive and Sexual Health (ARSH) program, the MedEngage platform has continued to expand the Company’s social impact, touching the lives of thousands across India.
At the core of Metropolis lies a clear and enduring purpose: 
“Healing the world, one diagnosis at a time”. Every sample, every report, and every interaction is grounded in the Company’s commitment to merging scientific excellence

EMERGING TRENDS IN DIAGNOSTIC INDUSTRY
Digital and AI-Driven Diagnostics
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) 
are transforming diagnostic workflows by enhancing image analysis, pattern recognition, and predictive modelling. These technologies are significantly improving accuracy and turnaround times in radiology, pathology, and genomics. Metropolis has invested in AI-powered platforms to facilitate earlier disease detection and streamline clinical reporting, reinforcing our commitment to data-driven diagnostics.
Decentralization of Care through Home-Based 
Services
Post-pandemic shifts have normalized home-based 
diagnostics and remote care. Services ranging from at-home sample collection to portable ECG and vitals testing are now common, especially in Tier II, Tier III, and rural areas. This decentralization improves access and convenience, bridging gaps in historically underserved regions. Metropolis is leveraging this trend through its expanding wellness-at-home offerings and localized service hubs to ensure quality care delivery anytime, anywhere.
Acceleration of Point-of-Care and At-Home 
Diagnostics
The demand for rapid, consumer-centric diagnostics 
continues to rise. Point-of-care testing (POCT) and at-home kits now go beyond traditional use cases like glucose and pregnancy testing. They encompass a broad range of tests, including infectious diseases, lipid profiles, and cardiac markers. These solutions provide timely, actionable insights with minimal infrastructure, aligning well with evolving consumer expectations and regulatory support.
Personalized and Predictive Diagnostics
Healthcare delivery is transitioning from reactive to proactive models. AI-enabled analytics now harness longitudinal patient data, behavioral insights, and routine lab results to predict disease risks and guide preventive care. Metropolis’ proprietary “Next Best Action” (NBA) framework exemplifies this shift –helping clinicians interpret both routine and advanced parameters to drive better health outcomes. Personalized diagnostics are a cornerstone of precision medicine and patient empowerment.
Expansion of Specialized and High-Value Testing
Rising incidences of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as cancer, cardiovascular disorders, and neurological conditions have accelerated the need for advanced testing modalities. High-complexity diagnostics—such as next-generation sequencing (NGS), molecular pathology, and liquid biopsy—enable early, precise, and actionable insights. Metropolis continues to invest in this space to strengthen our high-value testing portfolio and support clinicians in managing complex health conditions.
Industry Consolidation and Ecosystem Integration
The diagnostics sector is undergoing consolidation, with large players acquiring regional laboratories to enhance operational scale and geographic reach. Partnerships across health-tech, pharma, and public health sectors are fostering integrated healthcare ecosystems. Metropolis is strategically aligning with this trend through selective collaborations and M&A initiatives to optimize service delivery and expand our national footprint.
MAJOR GROWTH DRIVERS AND OPPORTUNITIES
Rising Burden of Non-Communicable Diseases 
(NCDs)
India is witnessing a surge in lifestyle-related and chronic 
conditions such as diabetes, cancer, cardiovascular, and respiratory disorders. These NCDs account for over two-thirds of all deaths and are expected to cost India US$
 
3.55 trillion in lost economic output between 2012 
and 20301. This shift is fuelling demand for specialized and 
high-frequency diagnostic testing, including preventive screenings and high-value pathology and radiology services. To meet this need, Metropolis has expanded its specialized testing portfolio, leveraging capabilities in Next Generation Sequencing (NGS), molecular diagnostics, and liquid biopsies through its dedicated Innovation Cell, addressing early disease detection and precision diagnostics.

health monitoring and age-specific diagnostics is expected to grow substantially. This demographic transformation is increasing the incidence of age-related ailments, expanding the market for chronic care and wellness testing. Tier II and Tier III Market Expansion
Tier II and Tier III cities in India represent a high-potential growth frontier for the diagnostics industry. These regions, characterized by limited diagnostic infrastructure and increasing healthcare needs, are witnessing a surge in demand for accessible and affordable testing services. Rising health awareness, greater insurance penetration, and digital connectivity are enabling consumers in smaller towns to seek timely diagnostics, particularly for preventive and chronic care. At Metropolis, the Company has scaled its reach across 750+ towns by end of FY25 and is pursuing deeper penetration through a structured franchise model. With supportive government policies and cost-effective expansion models, these markets are expected to play a pivotal role in driving inclusive and sustainable growth for the sector.
Health Insurance Penetration and Affordability
Greater access to health insurance is improving the affordability of diagnostics, especially among the middle and lower-income groups. Government initiatives like Ayushman Bharat and the National Health Mission have increased health coverage, enabling more individuals to access quality diagnostic services. This has reduced reliance on out-of-pocket expenses and facilitated routine health screenings and disease management tests.
Rising Income Levels
India’s rising per capita income and expanding middle class are increasing the population’s ability and willingness to invest in healthcare. This has led to higher demand for preventive screenings, wellness check-ups, and specialized diagnostics. As health awareness improves across demographics, there is growing preference for quality and convenience in diagnostic services. Metropolis has responded to this demand through its premium wellness offerings and curated test panels such as TruHealth, which cater to both aspirational and health-conscious consumers across urban and semi-urban markets.
Government Support and PPPs
State-level health initiatives, public-private partnerships (PPPs), and schemes like Ayushman Bharat are strengthening healthcare access in smaller towns. Diagnostic players with strong compliance, accreditation, and technology capabilities are well-positioned to benefit from government-backed opportunities in rural and semi-urban healthcare delivery.
India’s Role in Bridging the Global Diagnostics Gap
India’s cost efficiency, scientific capabilities, and strong pathology expertise uniquely position it to address diagnostic accessibility challenges in regions such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. These geographies continue to face significant gaps in advanced testing infrastructure, creating an opportunity for India to emerge as a global diagnostics leader.
By leveraging digital platforms, cross-border logistics, and 
public-private collaborations with international healthcare bodies, India can extend its diagnostic services globally. Metropolis Healthcare has already established a presence in 5 countries in Africa and operates B2B services in over 12 countries. The company is now focused on expanding its global footprint through strategic partnerships, telehealth integration, and international sample processing, aiming to position itself as a key player in global diagnostics.

THREATS
Workforce Shortage and Skill Gaps
The diagnostics industry faces a growing shortage of 
skilled professionals such as pathologists, radiologists, lab technicians, and phlebotomists. This challenge is more severe in rural and semi-urban areas, where access to trained talent is limited, affecting both service quality and reach. Regulatory requirements for accredited labs to employ full-time qualified staff further increase hiring pressures. As technology in diagnostics continues to advance, there is a constant need for training and upskilling, adding to the strain on human resources.
High Capital Expenditure and Operational Costs
Maintaining competitiveness requires continuous investment in advanced diagnostic equipment and technologies, such as molecular diagnostics and high-end imaging modalities. These investments entail substantial capital expenditure and ongoing maintenance costs. Moreover, the need for specialized infrastructure and trained personnel to operate sophisticated equipment adds to operational expenses, potentially impacting profitability, especially for smaller and mid-sized diagnostic centres.
Supply Chain Vulnerabilities and Import Dependence
India's diagnostics industry heavily relies on imported reagents, equipment, and consumables, with estimates indicating that 70–80% of high-value medical devices are imported. This dependence exposes the sector to global supply chain disruptions, currency fluctuations, and geopolitical tensions, which can lead to shortages and increased costs. Encouraging domestic manufacturing through policy support and incentives is crucial to mitigate these risks and enhance self-reliance.

RISK MANAGEMENT
Metropolis Healthcare Limited adopts a structured, disciplined, and integrated approach to Risk Management, embedded within its overall governance and strategic decision-making processes. The Company’s Risk Management framework is designed to identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate a wide spectrum of risks that may impact its operational, financial, reputational, or compliance objectives. The primary objective of the Risk Management framework is to facilitate Digital Transformation Barriers and Data Security 
Concerns
While digitalization offers opportunities for improved 
efficiency and access, it also presents challenges. The digital divide between urban and rural areas limits the reach of telemedicine and digital diagnostic services. Furthermore, the increasing digitization of patient data raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. The absence of comprehensive data protection regulations heightens the risk of data breaches, potentially undermining patient trust and compliance with international standards.
Fragmented Regulatory Landscape and Compliance 
Challenges
The regulatory environment for diagnostics in India is 
characterized by fragmentation and inconsistency. Only a limited number of states have adopted the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010, leading to varied standards and enforcement levels across regions. This inconsistency complicates compliance for diagnostic providers operating in multiple jurisdictions and may affect the standardization and quality of diagnostic services.
Prevalence of Unregulated and Substandard 
Laboratories
A significant number of diagnostic laboratories operate 
without proper accreditation or qualified personnel, leading to concerns about the accuracy and reliability of diagnostic results. The existence of such unregulated entities undermines public trust in diagnostic services and poses risks to patient safety. Strengthening regulatory oversight and enforcing quality standards are essential to address this issue.

5.   
  Specific commitments, goals and targ
ets set by the entity with 
defined timelines, if any.As a responsible and forward-looking organization, we are fully aligned with the principles of the National Guidelines on Responsible Business Conduct (NGRBC). Our commitment to sustainability is reflected in the way we approach environmental stewardship, diversity and inclusion, quality of care, and corporate governance.
We have set clear, measurable goals across ten key focus areas and will regularly 
report our progress to ensure transparency and accountability. Among our top environmental priorities, we aim to achieve carbon neutrality by 2043 and reduce emissions intensity by 45% by 2030. We are also committed to achieving zero waste across all our offices by 2030 and cutting plastic usage by half. In terms of water conservation, our targets include a 30% reduction in water intensity by 2030 and achieving water neutrality by 2043.
In the area of patient care and service excellence, we aim to resolve 100% of 
customer complaints registered in our CRM systems every year, while striving to maintain a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 90% by 2028—a testament to our commitment to consistently high service standards.
We are equally focused on building an inclusive and skilled workforce. Our goals 
include providing 100% of employees with training in Occupational Health & Safety (OHS) and ISO 15189, as well as achieving gender balance in our workforce with a 50:50 ratio by 2028.
Data privacy and security remain a top priority, and we are committed to 
maintaining zero data breaches year-on-year, supported by continued compliance with ISO 27001 and 27701 standards.
Furthermore, our efforts extend to community impact, where we plan to positively 
touch the lives of at least 600,000 beneficiaries by 2043. To ensure resilience and preparedness, we conduct annual risk assessments and implement mitigation plans as part of our ongoing risk management strategy.
These initiatives underscore our holistic approach to responsible business, aimed 
at creating long-term value for our stakeholders and contributing meaningfully to society and the environment.Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (Contd.)

EI-1. Describe the processes for identifying key stakeholder groups of the entity.Metropolis Healthcare follows a structured and evolving process to identify and engage with its key stakeholder groups, 
in line with the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) framework. This process involves periodic assessments of stakeholders based on their influence on, and impact from, the Company’s operations.
Stakeholders are broadly classified into internal (e.g., employees) and external (e.g., patients, doctors, investors, suppliers, 
regulators, partners, and community organizations) groups. The Company uses diverse engagement methods including surveys, direct feedback, consultations, partnerships, and formal governance and reporting mechanisms.
To strengthen this framework, Metropolis collaborates with professional ESG consultants to adopt global best practices 
in stakeholder mapping and engagement. These efforts help align business goals with stakeholder expectations, identify material sustainability issues, and drive improvements in ESG performance.
Stakeholder engagement is central to Metropolis’ responsible growth journey, enabling it to remain responsive, inclusive, 
and future-ready.Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (Contd.)

Leadership Indicators
LI-1. Provide the processes for consultation between stakeholders and the Board on economic, environmental, and 
social topics or if consultation is delegated, how is feedback from such consultations provided to the Board.
At Metropolis Healthcare, discussions on ESG matters are initiated at the functional level, where business and 
departmental heads engage directly with relevant stakeholders. These interactions help surface critical insights and concerns related to economic, environmental, and social issues. Key takeaways from these dialogues are consolidated and reviewed by the Company’s Key Managerial Personnel (KMP). This structured feedback mechanism ensures that material stakeholder inputs are escalated appropriately and presented to the Board of Directors during periodic meetings. This process enables informed decision-making and ensures that the Board remains attuned to evolving stakeholder expectations and ESG priorities.
LI-2. Whether stakeholder consultation is used to support the identification and management of environmental, and 
social topics (Yes / No). If so, provide details of instances as to how the inputs received from stakeholders on these topics were incorporated into policies and activities of the entity.
Metropolis Healthcare has established a robust governance framework to drive its Environmental, Social, and Governance 
(ESG) agenda. Stakeholder consultation plays a vital role in shaping the Company’s sustainability strategy by helping identify, assess, and manage key environmental and social issues. As part of this process, the Company undertook a comprehensive digital materiality assessment using a double materiality approach. This involved active engagement with diverse stakeholder groups—including employees, investors, customers, and partners—to understand both the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (Contd.)
98
Annual Report 2024-25
=== page 102 ===
impact of the business on the environment and society, and the influence of external factors on business performance. 
In collaboration with an external ESG consultant, and drawing from stakeholder feedback, Metropolis developed a clearly defined ESG roadmap with measurable goals and targets. To ensure inclusivity and relevance, multiple workshops were conducted to gather deep insights from stakeholders across regions and functions. The outcomes of these consultations have been directly embedded into the Company’s ESG strategy, ensuring strong alignment with stakeholder expectations and sustainability priorities. This ongoing engagement enables the Board and leadership to remain agile and responsive to emerging ESG trends and risks, while strengthening long-term value creation.
LI-3. Provide details of instances of engagement with, and actions taken to, address the concerns of vulnerable/ 
marginalized stakeholder groups.
At present, the Company has not identified any specific vulnerable or marginalized groups within its stakeholder universe. 
However, it remains committed to inclusivity and will continue to assess stakeholder dynamics periodically to ensure that the needs of all segments, including potentially underrepresented groups, are recognized and addressed where relevant.

EI-8. Mechanisms to prevent adverse consequences to the complainant in discrimination and harassment cases.
Metropolis has established clear and effective mechanisms to prevent any adverse consequences for individuals who 
report cases of discrimination or harassment. These include:
•
  S
trict Prohibition of Harassment and Discrimination: All employees are regularly informed that any form of 
harassment, discrimination, or inappropriate conduct is strictly prohibited within the organization.
•
  Clear R
eporting Channels: Employees are provided with clear guidance on designated contact points for raising 
concerns or seeking support related to harassment or discrimination.
•
  Prot
ection Against Retaliation: The Company assures all complainants that they will not face any punitive action 
or retaliation for raising genuine concerns in good faith.
•
  T
imely and Impartial Investigations: All complaints are promptly and thoroughly investigated, ensuring objectivity, 
confidentiality, and fairness throughout the process.
•
  Manag
erial Accountability: Managers are trained to recognize, prevent, and act upon any form of harassment or 
discrimination, and are held accountable for maintaining a respectful work environment.
Metropolis enforces a zero-tolerance policy against both the initial misconduct and any form of retaliation. Violations 
are met with strict disciplinary action to uphold a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace for all.

We partner with government-authorized agencies to collect and dispose of biomedical waste safely and compliantly. disruption or discontinuation of essential diagnostic services. Additionally, in line with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, the Company promptly notifies stock exchanges of any material events that may impact its operations, ensuring transparency with all stakeholders.

 R elated Party Transactions
  Process and Appro val Mechanism: Your Company has 
developed a governance structure for approving and monitoring the transactions with the related parties. A process is rolled out where all the related parties are identified, and a list of related parties is prepared to ensure that no transactions with related parties are entered without prior approval of the Audit Committee. Additionally, all the related party transactions are reviewed by the Audit Committee and the Board on a quarterly basis. The Audit Committee also seeks for external certification, if required to ensure that the transactions are at arm’s length and in ordinary course of business. Audit Committee grants omnibus approval for transactions which are regular and routine in nature as per the criteria approved by the Board and special or event-based transactions are approved separately by the Audit Committee in line with Related Party Transaction Policy of the Company.

1. Brief outline on CSR & ESG P olicy of the Company:
 
 A
t Metropolis Healthcare Limited (“the Company” or “Metropolis”), contributing to society is a fundamental value. 
For over four decades, we have remained dedicated to enhancing the quality of life in the communities we serve. 
Our approach to Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is deeply aligned with our vision and mission, emphasizing not only business growth but also positive social impact.
 
 Our flagship CSR initiativ
es are closely aligned with key United Nations Sustainable Development Goals 
(SDGs), including:
 •
 Good Health and W
ell-being (SDG 3)
 •
 Quality E
ducation (SDG 4)
 •
 Gender E
quality (SDG 5)
 These f
ocus areas shape the foundation of all our CSR efforts.
 
 The C
ompany’s CSR & ESG Policy (“the Policy”), as approved by the Board of Directors, is available on the official 
Metropolis website. Our CSR initiatives are designed to align with and support the objectives outlined in this Policy.
 
 A k
ey initiative under our CSR framework is the foundation established by the CSR & ESG Committee, which focuses 
on empowering adolescent girls by providing accurate information on reproductive health and essential life skills. This initiative seeks to educate and enable adolescents to make informed decisions and lead empowered lives.
 
 Th
rough our preventive healthcare programs, we engage directly with communities to raise awareness about health 
and wellness, promoting the importance of preventive care for building a healthier society.
 
 Our 
flagship program, MedEngage, supports aspiring medical professionals by offering scholarships and research 
grants, nurturing the next generation of healthcare leaders.
 
 Me
tropolis consistently implements community-focused initiatives that deliver tangible and lasting impact, 
particularly in areas surrounding our operations. Our efforts prioritize underprivileged and marginalized communities, aiming to uplift and empower them. We remain committed to creating long-term stakeholder value by being socially responsible, inclusive, and focused on improving health, education, and overall well-being for all.

1. C OMPANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CODE OF GOVERNANCE
  Y our Company’s philosophy on Corporate Governance is based on a holistic approach not only towards its own 
growth but also towards maximization of benefits to the shareholders, employees, customers, government and 
also the general public at large. Transparency and accountability are the fundamental principles of sound Corporate Governance, which ensures that the organization is managed and monitored in a responsible manner for creating and sharing stakeholder’s value.
 
 Y
our Company is committed to good Corporate Governance and adherence to best practices at all times and its 
philosophy is based on five basic elements namely, accountability, value creation, strategic-guidance, transparency and equitable treatment to all stakeholders.
 
 Metropolis 
Healthcare Limited (“the Company”) believes in following values which serve as guiding principles for 
Company’s culture, decisions, and behaviour.
  
Precision: Driven by science and a commitment to accuracy, we deliver reliable diagnostics-with precision at the 
core of everything we do.
  C
ompassion: Placing empathy at the heart of healthcare, we ensure every individual feels cared for and respected-
because every test deserves a human touch.
  Ownership:
 Acting with accountability and initiative to uphold the trust placed in us-owning every step, every day, 
at every level.
2.  BO ARD OF DIRECTORS
 C
omposition of Board
  The Board represents appropriate mix of Executive, Non-Executive Directors and Independent Directors including 
one woman Independent Director which is in compliance with the requirements of Companies Act, 2013 ("the Act"), SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (“SEBI Listing Regulations”) and the Articles of Association of the Company. The Board composition represents an optimal mix of professionalism, knowledge, expertise and experience which enables the Board to discharge its responsibilities efficiently and provide effective leadership to the business. As on March 31, 2025, the Board of the Company comprises of 8 (eight) Directors of which 4 (four) are Non-Executive Independent Directors, 3 (three) are Non-Executive Non-Independent Directors and 1 (one) is Executive Director. Brief profile of the Directors is available on the website of the Company at https://www.metropolisindia.com/investors and also forms part of this Annual Report.
 Board and C ommittee Meetings
  The Board and C ommittee meetings are pre-scheduled. The schedule of the Board and Committee meetings is 
communicated to the Directors in advance to ensure their availability to attend the meetings. The Board Meeting is conducted at least once in every quarter to discuss the performance of the Company and its Quarterly Financial Results along with other Company matters. The agenda along with explanatory notes thereto of the business(es) to be transacted at the Board and Committee Meetings are circulated well in advance to the Board/respective Committees of the Company. Further, video-conferencing facilities are also provided to facilitate Directors travelling/residing abroad or at other locations to participate in the meetings. The necessary quorum was present for all the meetings. The Management team provides update on key areas such as business performance, functional outcomes etc. In case of urgent matters, approvals are sought by way of circular resolution.

the year under review, 6 (six) Board meetings were held and the gap between two meetings did not exceed

  C ode of Conduct for Board Members and Senior 
Management Personnel (‘Code’)
 
 T
he Company’s Code is the principal document 
which stems on the core values of the Company viz (i) Commitment to excellence; (ii) Integrity including intellectual honesty, openness, fairness and trust; (iii) Care for people; (iv) Socially-valued enterprise and (v) Business Integrity with focus to become a dynamic and successful business organization. All the Directors and Senior management are mandated to act honestly, fairly, ethically and with integrity, and conduct themselves in a professional, courteous and respectful manner. They are also mandated to provide annual affirmation on compliance with the Code.  The C ode is displayed on the website of the

 C onflict of Interest
  The C ompany has established a process to proactively 
identify and avoid conflicts of interest. As part of this process, each Director is required to disclose, on an annual basis or upon any change during the year, their interests in other entities, including Board and Committee Memberships/Chairmanships held in other companies. The Board members exercises due care and avoids any conflict of interest while discharging their duties, particularly in the decision-making process.
  P olicy on Related Party Transactions (‘RPT 
Policy’) 
  All transactions ent ered into with the Related Parties 
during financial year 2024-25 were in the ordinary course of business, and on an arm’s length basis and in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder, the SEBI Listing Regulations, and the Company’s RPT Policy. Further, the Company has not entered into a materially significant transaction with the Related Parties which attracts Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. As a process all the transactions with the Related Parties are placed before the Audit Committee for its approval and a statement of Related Party Transaction is also placed before the Audit Committee to ensure the transactions are within the limits approved by the Audit Committee.
 
 During the year under review
, the Audit Committee, 
as part of its periodic review cycle, reviewed the RPT policy at its meeting held on November 08, 2024, and recommended necessary amendments to the Board, which were subsequently approved by the Board. Corporate Governance Report (Contd.)

Independent Auditor’s Report
To the Members of Metropolis Healthcare Limited
Report on the Audit of the Standalone Financial 
Statements
Opinion
We have audited the standalone financial statements 
of Metropolis Healthcare Limited (the “Company”) which comprise the standalone balance sheet as at 31 March 2025, and the standalone statement of profit and loss (including other comprehensive income), standalone statement of changes in equity and standalone statement of cash flows for the year then ended, and notes to the standalone financial statements, including material accounting policies and other explanatory information.
In our opinion and to the best of our information and 
according to the explanations given to us, the aforesaid standalone financial statements give the information required by the Companies Act, 2013 (“Act”) in the manner so required and give a true and fair view in conformity with the accounting principles generally accepted in India, of 
the state of affairs of the Company as at 31 March 2025, and its profit and other comprehensive loss, changes in equity and its cash flows for the year ended on that date.
Basis for Opinion
We conducted our audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing (SAs) specified under Section
 
143(10) of the 
Act. Our responsibilities under those SAs are further described in the 
Auditor’s Responsibilities for the

Auditor’s Responsibilities for the Audit of the 
Standalone Financial Statements
Our objectives are to obtain reasonable assurance about 
whether the standalone financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue an auditor’s report that includes our opinion. Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance, but is not a guarantee that an audit conducted in accordance with SAs will always detect a material misstatement when it exists. Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these standalone financial statements.
As part of an audit in accordance with SAs, we exercise 
professional judgment and maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit. We also:
•  Identify and assess the risks of mat erial misstatement 
of the standalone financial statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform audit procedures responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion. The risk of not detecting a material misstatement resulting from fraud is higher than for one resulting from error, as fraud may involve collusion, forgery, intentional omissions, misrepresentations, or the override of internal control.
•  Obtain an understanding of int ernal control relevant 
to the audit in order to design audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances. Under Section 143(3)(i) of the Act, we are also responsible for expressing our opinion on whether the company has adequate internal financial controls with reference to financial statements in place and the operating effectiveness of such controls.
•  E valuate the appropriateness of accounting
